clue.text: The same check is catching firm making a birdhouse

indicators.note: to catch something is to take hold of it, so one piece closes around another

blocks.note: DO is short for ditto, meaning the same again
to vet is to check over
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An inspector checks that a firm is building identical birdhouses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The same' is not a definition here: ditto is abbreviated DO, a convention worth learning. 'Is catching' means the check wraps around the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovecot is a small structure built to house pigeons or doves, so a birdhouse is a fair general description.

clue.text: Austrian physicist, active person, adopting very quiet line

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one piece takes others inside it

blocks.note: someone who acts, a doer
pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A description of an energetic Austrian scientist who took up a quiet line of work.
explanation.walkthrough: DOER takes in PP and L: DO(PPL)ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian Doppler was the nineteenth-century Austrian scientist who described the frequency shift named after him.

clue.text: An excess of words for this in an anagram?

blocks.note: surface reading: a name for talking far too much
setter's reading: in an anagram the letters of words run loose, a digestive joke about language

explanation.surface: Asking what we call a flood of words, and what an anagram might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half plays on the phrase: letters in an anagram are loose, so an anagram is a kind of runny word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone who talks incessantly, producing a needless torrent of speech.

clue.text: Rector in church suspended about half of LP record

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around another
half of a two-letter item is just one of its letters, the opening one here

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
R is the abbreviation for rector
on ice means put on hold, suspended
the first of the two letters

explanation.surface: A rector has been suspended over a church matter concerning a vinyl album.
explanation.walkthrough: Rector sits in the clue first, but CH then R reads in the answer; ON ICE (suspended) wraps around L: CH + R + ON IC(L)E.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a historical account of events, so a record in the noun sense.

clue.text: Corporation getting billions after introducing hard part of glove

indicators.note: to introduce is to bring in, so one piece is put inside another

blocks.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a paunch, a tum
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
B is the abbreviation for billions

explanation.surface: A corporation earns billions by bringing out a tough glove.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation looks like a business but is an old word for a big belly: T(H)UM, then B after.
explanation.definitionFit: A glove has a separate sheath for each digit, and the thumb is one of those sections.

clue.text: Strongly smelling substance affected half of horses

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word keeps only its opening three letters

blocks.note: camp means theatrically affected
the first letter, second letter and third letter of the six, its front half

explanation.surface: A pungent substance has affected half the horses in a stable.
explanation.walkthrough: Affected looks like a verb, but it is the adjective meaning showy and mannered, CAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Camphor is a waxy aromatic compound with a sharp medicinal odour, used in mothballs and liniments.

clue.text: Object to everybody entering cold prehistoric area

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it

blocks.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
everybody, all
a henge is a prehistoric circular enclosure like Stonehenge

explanation.surface: People protest at everybody crowding into a chilly ancient site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prehistoric area' points to a henge, the ring of earthworks or stones best known from Stonehenge in Wiltshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To challenge a claim or decision is to dispute it, a verb synonym for objecting.

clue.text: Significant expression of surprise about lunch?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise
to lunch is to eat, an example shown by the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone gasps at an impressive lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Lunch is read as a verb: to lunch is one way to EAT, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meaty has substance and weight, like a meaty debate, so significant in that figurative sense.

clue.text: Once and for all a hit, I fancy?

definitions.text: Once and for all a hit, I fancy?

indicators.note: fancy can mean elaborately decorated or made over, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wistful guess that something was a hit once and for all.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder skips 'and'. Read whole, the clue describes the Eagles' hit song, a place you check into once and for all: you can check out but never leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1977 Eagles single was a huge hit, and its lyric famously says guests can never leave.

clue.text: Work steadily after harvest to try again

blocks.note: to reap is to harvest
to ply a trade is to work at it steadily

explanation.surface: A farm worker keeps going after the harvest before trying again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the work piece behind the harvest piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To reapply is to submit another application, as for a job, which means making another attempt.

clue.text: Difficulty in getting up in an ancient language

definitions.text: Difficulty in getting up in an ancient language

blocks.note: surface reading: trouble rising from bed in the morning
setter's reading: a Latin motto about rising to the heavens through hardship

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to get up, or describes doing so in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin motto means 'through adversity to the stars'; getting up is soaring into the sky, not leaving bed.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the motto of the Royal Air Force, the British military flying service, meaning through hardship to the stars.

clue.text: Comprehend inclination to bag runs

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it in a sack, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a lean is a slope or inclination
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A batter comes to understand the knack of scoring runs.
explanation.walkthrough: Inclination is a physical slant here, not a desire.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn something is to come to grasp or understand it, so the verbs are near synonyms.

clue.text: Call carvery at last: turkey? It’s not what you would call swan!

definitions.text: It’s not what you would call swan!

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the preceding word

blocks.note: to give someone a bell is British slang for a phone call
its final letter
a turkey is a failure, a flop

explanation.surface: A diner shouting at a carvery about the turkey and swan on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The food words mislead: turkey is a failed show and a swan is a graceful swan dive.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy dive landing flat on the stomach is the opposite of an elegant swan dive.

clue.text: Republican intervention - item that’s edited out?

blocks.note: red is the colour of the US Republican party
an intervention is taking action

explanation.surface: A political party steps in and something gets cut from a document.
explanation.walkthrough: Republican is usually just R, but here it is RED, the party's colour on US election maps.
explanation.definitionFit: A redaction is a passage blacked out or removed from a document before publication, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Pub and church restricting chimney’s sway

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so pieces close around another

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
CE is the Church of England
a flue is a chimney duct

explanation.surface: A pub and a church are both stopping a chimney from swaying.
explanation.walkthrough: INN and CE together hold FLUE: IN(FLUE)N + CE. Sway is the noun for power, not swinging.
explanation.definitionFit: Sway as a noun means power or control over others, a synonym for influence.

clue.text: Study year all set to go

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A student's year of study is about to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: To read a subject at university is British usage for studying it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fully prepared for departure or action is what ready means.

clue.text: Supporting justice is tougher, unfortunately

indicators.note: something that turns out unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters go awry

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Backing the cause of justice is regrettably harder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporting justice' reads like a description of a cause, but it is the definition; the letters of 'is tougher' do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A righteous person is morally upright and on the side of fairness and law.

clue.text: Tower to be evacuated? Excellent suggestion

indicators.note: evacuating empties out the interior, leaving only the outside letters

blocks.note: its outer letters
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: Someone proposes clearing a tower and is praised for the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Suggestion here means a faint hint, not a proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace is a tiny amount or slight hint, as in a suggestion of garlic.

clue.text: Leading politician blocking most admired person for key spot on board?

indicators.note: something blocking a channel sits in the middle of it

blocks.note: the toast of the town is the person most admired
the Prime Minister leads the government

explanation.surface: A senior politician stands in the way of a celebrity in a boardroom.
explanation.walkthrough: On board means aboard ship, not on a company board.
explanation.definitionFit: The topmast is the upper section of a ship's mast, a prominent position above the deck.

clue.text: Small bird hurried to good heather

blocks.note: fled, ran away fast
G is the abbreviation for good
ling is another name for heather

explanation.surface: A little bird flitted across to some fine heather.
explanation.walkthrough: LING as heather is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A fledgling is a young bird that has just grown its flight feathers, so a small one.

clue.text: Old American seen around North Arkansas food store

indicators.note: something seen around another thing surrounds it

blocks.note: a Gray was a Confederate soldier in the American Civil War
N is the abbreviation for north
AR is the postal code for Arkansas

explanation.surface: An elderly American is spotted near a shop in northern Arkansas.
explanation.walkthrough: Old American is not a pensioner but a Civil War Confederate, the side that wore grey.
explanation.definitionFit: A granary is a storehouse for threshed grain, so a building that stores food.

clue.text: Film company having value after good performance of course?

blocks.note: par is the standard score on a golf course
an amount is a value or sum

explanation.surface: A studio is valued after a strong performance, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like 'naturally' but means on a golf course, where a sound score for a hole is the standard one.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount Pictures is one of the major Hollywood studios.

clue.text: Film version that is suppressed by Missouri

blocks.note: MO is the postal code for Missouri
V is the abbreviation for version
i.e. means that is

explanation.surface: A version of a film has been banned in Missouri.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, being suppressed by MO means sitting beneath it. 'That' alone gives IE (that is).
explanation.definitionFit: Movie is the everyday American word for a cinema picture, a synonym for film.

clue.text: A lot of attempts to keep time may be unconvincing

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the tail goes
to keep something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: tries, missing its last letter
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Repeated attempts to keep to time may come across as unpersuasive.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIES loses its S, then holds T: TRI(T)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite remarks are hackneyed and stale, and so they fail to persuade anyone.

clue.text: Norse girl that mostly welcomes soldiers

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
to welcome someone is to take them in

blocks.note: the word without its last letter
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian girl who generally makes troops welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) for soldiers is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Thora is a female name of Old Norse origin, derived from the god Thor.

clue.text: In a romantic move, dropping English, I garbled romantic Latin phrase

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it go, so a letter is removed
garbled means jumbled and confused, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, less the E
E is the abbreviation for English, the letter removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Making a romantic gesture, someone mangles a famous Latin love line.
explanation.walkthrough: Take E out of the first four words, add I, and shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase from Virgil means love conquers all, so it is a famously romantic saying.

clue.text: Skill in twirling shown by last character in number one circus act

indicators.note: something twirling spins round, so it ends up facing back the other way
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: art is skill
number one is a childish word for urinating, a pee
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An acrobat's spinning skill shown off in the final part of a headline circus routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Number one is not first place but childish slang for a wee; Z goes inside it after the turned ART.
explanation.definitionFit: The trapeze is an aerial swing used by circus acrobats, and the term also names their act.

clue.text: City of London to stop importing second drug

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: EC is the postcode district for the City of London
to stay a process is to halt it
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: The City of London trying to halt a drug from being brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London is the capital's financial district, and its postcodes begin EC; 'to stop' is the verb 'stay', as in staying an execution.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is the street name for MDMA, an illegal recreational stimulant.
